15sept1610.summary: Marie de Médicis to Brèves, two ciphered passages on Savoy's son's journey to Spain: their persistence in raising difficulties "will show too plainly their malice and ambition", which she judges would be "accompanied by imprudence and weakness" given the present state of their affairs.
15sept1610.en:
If on top of that they still raise difficulties about it, it will be showing too plainly their malice and ambition,
which I judge, should it come to action, must be accompanied by imprudence and [?by] weakness, given the present state
of their affairs.

10nov1610.summary: In mid-sentence, on Savoy's disarmament after Henri IV's death and Spain's refusal: "the pope, recognising their arrogance and sensing his own timidity", would not press Spain to the point of disarmament only to receive the shame of a flat refusal.
10nov1610.en:
So I see clearly that the Pope, [?recognising] their arrogance and feeling his own timidity, [would] not be pressed to
the extremity of disarmament only to receive in the end the shame of an absolute refusal.

lasry-additional.summary: A letter in the same key, read by George Lasry (CTTS, 2022; improved with Opus 5.5, Oct 2026): marriage negotiations under aliases (La Hale, Le Cormier, La Cheville, Pindare, Saint Paul). Shelfmark and date not established; it may be Henri IV to Brèves (R2077), but Lasry asks that it not be identified with R2077 without a matching archival image.
lasry-additional.en:
La Hale and le Cormier are [still?] pursuing at Pi[75̄] the negotiations begun for the marriages of their daughters
with la Cheville, and I see so far that the first has already gained the better part over the other. Everything in
this regard is still intact. The talk of that of Pindare with la Cheville was renewed again these past days by the
[means?; 48̄] of Pic[75̄]; of which the one of [l'Olivier?], having got wind of it, came to find me and point out not
only the displeasure that the [means?; 48̄] of le Gris de Lin would feel at it, but the just jealousy that the one of
Saint Paul would conceive of it, with the prejudice that this new suit might bring to the alliance lately contracted
with Saint Felix, with other similar reasons and considerations, to put me off listening to the overture of that of le
Bateur.

snip.cap: F. 19r, 10 November 1610: the cipher after Aussi vois-je bien, opening with barred 72 (que), 4 (le pape) and barred 79 (re)

system: Henri IV-Brèves cipher of 1610 (key BnF fr. 3462, Gallica view 112): homophonic alphabet of 2-5 signs per letter, comma-marked letter codes for common words, plain and overbarred number codes.
